V2.4 FOLLOW-01, 2026-08-26 — ONE new spec file, MEASURED LOCALLY, and the partition COUNT raised on the arithmetic rather than the coverage trimmed. `follow-01-week-account.spec.ts` is 43.2 s over 4 tests, measured in the sandbox that produced the change from a green run of the file, with `--as local/v2.4-follow-01`. Every other spec file's duration is untouched; 117 of them still read `ci:32605964327` and two read `local/v2.4-gate-02`. The first CI run that publishes this file's artifact should replace it with `ci:<run id>`.

PARTITION_COUNT moved 12 → 13, and this is the question V2.4-GATE-02 told the next item adding E2E coverage to confront. The arithmetic: with the new file measured in, twelve partitions derive a heaviest of 1007.7 s = 16.80 min against the 16.73 min ceiling `MAX_PARTITION_SECONDS` derives — and it does not fail by a rounding error, because the MEAN of the ten non-sliced partitions is already 1005.0 s, so no packing of any 43-second file fits and reaching the ceiling would mean deleting about a third of the new coverage. Thirteen derives a heaviest of 918.7 s = 15.31 min, 68% of `globalTimeout` — the same target every split since HARDEN-04 has been tuned to. The ceiling was NOT raised; that is the one answer HARDEN-04 removed from the table.

The new coverage was sized before the count moved, not instead of moving it: the FOLLOW-01 journey was consolidated from 6 tests over 11 page loads to 4 over 8, asserting the same things — what was removed is redundant page LOADS (a second navigation to re-open the same account at another width, and a separate visit for the Review's phone tier, both now resizes in place), never an assertion.

The COST of thirteen, stated: ~2.3 min more runner time on setup that buys no coverage, and one job past the pool figure interpolated from run 31445526789 — which measured EIGHTEEN shards queueing, not thirteen, while run 32333645709 measured twelve starting within ONE SECOND of each other with none queued. If the interpolation is right the failure mode is bounded and already written down in `PARTITION_COUNT`: a queued job costs WALL CLOCK and nothing else, because a job that has not started spends none of its `globalTimeout`.

The BETTER fix, measured and deliberately not taken here. `responsive.spec.ts` is 1471.6 s in one generated matrix file and `--shard` is the only way to divide it, so it takes two EXCLUSIVE partitions of 735.8 s apiece against a 1004 s ceiling — stranding 536 s, 8.9 minutes, of gate capacity that no partition can use, which is why twelve looked exhausted. Recovering it needs either a redesign of `derivePartitions` (both shards of a sliced group must carry an IDENTICAL spec list, or tests are lost and duplicated) or a near-50/50 split of that file into two real spec files. Both change what every partition holds. Raised as its own PRODUCT_DEBT entry with these numbers so the next pass takes it deliberately.
